recap: In the season curtain-opener, Sanfrecce Hiroshima visited newly promoted V-Varen Nagasaki - a 20-munite 3-goal blitz either side of half time
proved a rude welcome back to the big time. The new format of the J1 league was on show as Vissel Kobe visited Kyoto Sanga - a 1-1 deadlock after normal time
was settled on penalties, with Kobe scoring 4 in a row to grab the 2 points. Machida Zelvia impressed in a 2-3 away win at Yokohama F. Marinos, an Erik double
providing the perfect away performance. Away sides continued to prosper on MD1 as Urawa Reds came away with all 3 points from their trip to J1 new boys JEF United,
2 goals in the first 12 minutes settling the game before a contest could emerge. Penalties all round as reigning champions Kashima Antlers came unstuck at FC Tokyo,
a 1-1 draw in normal time giving way to an intense 5-4 shootout, with FC Tokyo emerging victorious. A similar story occured in the Osaka derby - a feisty competition
saw both teams reduced to 10 men, but it was Gamba who triumphed over Cerezo on penalties, securing the 2 on the back of a 5-4 shootout win. More joy from the spot
for the wasps of Avispa Fukuoka, who snuck past Fagiano Okayama 6-5 in the highest scoring shootout of the weekend after another 1-1 draw. No such worries for
Nagoya - Yudai Kimura netting the winner in a 1-0 win over Shimizu S-Pulse. Perhaps the game of the weekend was at Kawasaki - a thrilling 5-3 win over Kashiwa
Reysol after a hat-trick from Brazilian superstar Erison. Elsewhere Mito Hollyhock made it 3 out of 3 losses for the newly-promoted sides, falling 3-1 away to
notoriously goal-shy Tokyo Verdy.
Vissel Kobe started the matchday with a routine 2-0 win over V-Varen, who remain pointless. Sanfrecce overcame 10-man Okayama on penalties after yet another 1-1 draw
in regulation time. A similar story between S-Pulse and Kyoto Sanga, with Sanga bouncing back from an opening weekend loss on pens to grab a 3-1 shootout victory.
Yet another game decided by penalties between Machida Zelvia and Mito Hollyhock, after an extraordinary last 5 minutes of the first half saw each side score twice -
the rest of the game remained goalless until Machida's 4-2 win from the spot. Kashima Antlers recovered from their MD1 loss to beat Yokohama F. Marinos 1-0, 2025 MVP
Leo Ceara proving the matchwinner. The vanquishers of Kashima on MD1, FC Tokyo, repeated the trick with another shootout win after a 1-1 draw - Urawa Reds the unlucky
victims this time around. An faintly ridiculous 9-8 shootout between JEF United and Kawasaki Frontale gave Kawasaki the win after a drab 0-0. Tokyo Verdy continued
their unlikely strong start by visting 10-man Kashiwa Reysol and coming away 2-1 victors. Cerezo Osaka took all 3 points from Avispa Fukuoka after a regulation 2-0 win.
Closing out the matchday, Gamba Osaka secured their second 2-point shootout victory after sharing a goalless draw with Nagoya, this time 3-2.
Urawa Reds got back to winning ways, plundering all 3 points from a 2-0 visit to Yokohama F. Marinos. Tokyo Verdy came from 2 goals down in the last 5 minutes
to deny Mito Hollyhock their first victory - rubbed salt in Hollyhock wounds by securing a 4-3 win on penalties. Shimizu S-Pulse got off the mark by scraping
past Vissel Kobe 1-0, with Kobe having to play over 70 minutes with 10 men after Tetsushi Yamakawa's red card. V-Varen Nagasaki pulled off a superb away win in
Nagoya, Norman Cambell's double paving the way for a 3-1 win. FC Tokyo also took all 3 points from a visit to Kawasaki, ending up 2-1 winners. Kashima Antlers
are starting to build momentum - overpowering Kashiwa Reysol 2-0 in a meeting of last season's top 2. Gamba Osaka came from a goal down to snatch victory from
a trip to Okayama, who remain winless. A season-first clash between 2 newly promoted teams saw Mito Hollyhock take a shootout win from the visit of JEF United,
a 5-3 shootout win coming after a 1-1 deadlock in normal time. Kyoto Sanga took a regulation home win over Avispa Fukuoka, Brazilians Rafael Elias and Marco Tulio
scoring each side of half time. Sanfrecce Hiroshima continued their good start to the tournament by snatching a 97th minute winner to take maximum points from
Cerezo Osaka - Solomon's 95th minute bicycle kick equaliser coming to nothing in the end as Shunki Higashi stole the win for the three arrows.
